Pricing automation tools is harder than it should be. Each platform bills a different unit, and most VPS deals advertise a price you only pay for the first term. Here's what I learned. All prices were checked on 16 Oct 2026.
Zapier bills tasks. Each successful action step is one task. Triggers and built-in tools like Filter, Formatter and Paths don't count. A 5-step Zap that runs once uses 5 tasks.

articles.author: andreagomez
articles.description:
Authenticating WebSocket connections at the edge


A WebSocket session begins as an ordinary HTTP request and stops being one after the server answers with 101 Switching Protocols. Authentication middleware, reverse proxies and web application firewalls get one chance to inspect that request. After the upgrade they see a long-lived TCP connection carrying frames they usually do not parse. Teams that protect REST endpoints carefully often leave the socket path to whatever the framework does by default.
RFC 6455 defines the opening handshake, including Upgrade: websocket, Sec-WebSocket-Key and Sec-WebSocket-Version: 13. Because the handshake is an HTTP request, it carries cookies and an Authorization header when the client chooses to send them. That is where a session check belongs.

articles.description:
To monitor cron job silent failure, use app logs and an external heartbeat together, then keep a durable run record that survives rollback. The deciding constraint is simple: a nightly developer-tools pipeline can fail before its code emits a single log line. Logs explain work that ran; heartbeat monitoring detects work that never appeared.
TL;DR: Treat the scheduler, the job, and the monitor as three failure domains. Send a start signal, write structured progress logs, commit a success record only after the output is durable, and let an independent deadline watcher flag a missing success. During rollback, preserve the same run ID and monitor contract so the evidence remains comparable across releases.
A log search answers questions about events that reached the log path. It cannot disting…
